clue.text: A person could well be put out by it

definitions.text: A person could well be put out by it

parts.words: A person could well be put out by it
parts.note: put out reads as annoyed or inconvenienced, but here it means rendered unconscious, as a patient is before surgery

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests irritation; the real sense is knocked out by a drug given before an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that removes sensation or consciousness is exactly what puts a patient out before surgery.

clue.text: A really quiet rest can bring calm

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
ease is rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: Peace and quiet with a good rest can soothe a person.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is pianissimo, the musical instruction for very quiet playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify someone is to settle or soothe them, restoring calm.

clue.text: Make war or bolt

indicators.note: make tells us to build something new out of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A choice between fighting and running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' signals rearranging WAR and OR together; 'bolt' looks like a verb for fleeing but is a crossbow missile.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow bolt is a short heavy missile shot from a bow, like a shaft.

clue.text: Domestic storage not yet filled up

definitions.meaning: a household room where preserves, liqueurs and cakes were kept and prepared in a large house
there is still space available, nothing full yet

explanation.definitionFit: A pantry-like room in a big house held provisions; and a space not full still has capacity left.

clue.text: A top man gets a key

parts.note: he is a pronoun standing for a man
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: The boss is given a key to the building.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' is a link word; the second 'a' supplies a letter. D is one of the musical keys.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest part or the leader of something is its uppermost point.

clue.text: The most delicious wine in the try-out

indicators.note: in means the wine sits inside the word for try-out

parts.note: a try-out is a test or trial
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Picking the best wine at a tasting session.
explanation.walkthrough: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative of flavourful: the most appetising to eat or drink.

clue.text: Having caught some fish, hold on

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler who has landed a fish keeps a firm grip on it.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scorecards; ling is an Atlantic food fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip tightly and refuse to let go is to hang on.

clue.text: A city company records gaining a couple of points

indicators.note: gaining means the records take on the points at their end

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
N and E are two compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: A firm's records gain a few marks of improvement in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points N, E, S and W are standard crossword letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A large German city on the Rhine is one example of an urban centre.

clue.text: Clement is the one who'll exhibit this

definitions.text: Clement is the one who'll exhibit this

parts.words: Clement is the one who'll exhibit this
parts.note: Clement looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning merciful or mild, and a merciful person shows mildness in judging

explanation.walkthrough: The capital C disguises the adjective 'clement' (mild, merciful) as a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Clemency and mercy are the quality of not being harsh in punishment.

clue.text: Workers following political leader they support

indicators.note: following means the workers come after the political letter
the leader of the word political is its opening letter

parts.note: artisans are skilled manual workers

explanation.surface: Labourers backing the head of their party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Political leader' looks like a party chief, but it is only the first letter of 'political'.
explanation.definitionFit: Committed backers of a cause or faction are its adherents.

clue.text: Thought Latin best

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A scholar thinks the classical language was the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect, the most suitable possible, is the optimum.

clue.text: There's a dandy here too

parts.note: a swell is a fashionably dressed man, a dandy

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a fashionable gentleman is also present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' is old slang for a smartly dressed man; split differently the letters make a phrase meaning also.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase means also or in addition.

clue.text: Give voice repeatedly and jail's the result!

indicators.note: repeatedly means the singing word is written out twice

parts.note: to sing is to give voice

explanation.surface: Endless singing gets someone locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a famous maximum-security prison in New York State; 'sing' is also slang for informing on criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: A New York State prison whose name is a byword for confinement.

clue.text: A journalist's alternative after reversing the drift

indicators.note: after places the alternative behind the reversed drift
reversing means the word for drift is read backwards

parts.note: a tide is a drift or current, as in the tide of opinion
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A reporter offers another option after turning the conversation round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' turns TIDE into EDIT, and OR goes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who prepares copy for a newspaper is a member of the press.

clue.text: Put in this month — date to be arranged

parts.note: inst., instant, is the old business abbreviation for this month

indicators.note: to be arranged tells us the letters of date are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An entry for this month with the date yet to be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be arranged' rearranges DATE as ATED. INST (instant) was formal letter-writing shorthand for the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone in an office is to establish them there.

clue.text: May be made sergeant, thereby causing split

definitions.note: the -ing phrase stands for the verb, to cause a split

indicators.note: may be made says the letters of sergeant can be made into something else

explanation.surface: Promoting someone to sergeant could create division in the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be made' rearranges the letters of SERGEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people from each other is to drive a wedge between them.

clue.text: Don't forget about prayer

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a collect is a short prayer in Christian liturgy

explanation.surface: A reminder to remember one's prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect is a short set prayer, stressed on the first syllable; RE means 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember is to call back to mind rather than lose a memory.

clue.text: In favour of charge for report

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a claim is a charge or demand, as a claim against someone

explanation.surface: Supporting a charge for a written report.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce publicly is to make an official declaration.

clue.text: Girls seen together in the garden

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Two young women spotted side by side among the flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Two girls' names joined make a herb grown in gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic herb that is commonly grown among garden plants.

clue.text: Run over a note on evidence

indicators.note: on means the note sits on top of the evidence in this down entry

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a trace is a sign or evidence left behind

explanation.surface: A detective's memo about the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts RE above TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back over a route or steps again is to retread it.

clue.text: A joint without credit? That's a good one!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the joint goes round the credit

parts.note: a seam is a joint where two pieces meet

explanation.surface: Someone jokes about a pub meal served with no payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, an old sense, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A very funny person or thing is said to be a riot or a hoot.

clue.text: Aquatic creature providing the human race with a starting-point

parts.note: man means mankind, the human race
a tee is the starting-point of each golf hole

explanation.surface: A sea animal giving humanity somewhere to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The tee is where each hole of golf begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A large plant-eating sea mammal, the sea cow, lives in water.

clue.text: The agitated star can't perform

indicators.note: agitated means the letters of the following words are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: The nervous celebrity is unable to go on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' rearranges STAR CANT; the apostrophe adds no letter. 'Perform' here means to carry out business, not act.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct or carry out a deal is to execute it.

clue.text: Some students at educational establishments are overfed

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complaint that pupils at schools are given too much food.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'establishments are overfed' as the definition, but only 'overfed' defines the answer; 'establishments' belongs to the surface phrase hiding it and 'are' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Having eaten more than enough is being satiated or glutted.

clue.text: Tart about travel, showing bottle

indicators.note: about means the tart is placed around the travel word

parts.note: a flan is an open tart
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A pastry carried on a journey, alongside a jug of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts the tart FLAN round GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A large vessel with a handle and spout for wine or ale is a jug or pitcher.

clue.text: In the lake district a river can look great!

definitions.text: In the lake district a river

indicators.note: can look suggests the letters of great can take on another appearance

explanation.surface: Scenery in the Lakes looking magnificent beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a mountainous area of north-west England; a short river there bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cumbrian river flowing near Keswick is one waterway of that region.

clue.text: Profit from article in spirit

indicators.note: in means the article is placed inside the spirit

parts.note: gin is a spirit
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Making money from a story printed in a ghostly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial benefit or earnings come from a successful dealing.

clue.text: The French male is into creative work, being bright

indicators.note: is into means the French word goes inside the creative work

parts.note: art is creative work
le is the French masculine form of the

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is interested in painting, being clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is into' puts LE, the masculine French for 'the', inside ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick-witted and watchful, as a sharp mind is attentive.

clue.text: A returning sailor set about people — for shame!

indicators.note: returning means the word for sailor is read backwards

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: about means the set goes around the people

parts.note: taken as written
men are people

explanation.surface: A sailor coming home and attacking people is a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns AB into BA; 'about' puts MEN inside SET to give SEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Humiliation, being degraded or brought low, is a state of disgrace.

clue.text: Show how little devils treat twister

parts.note: demons are devils, the little suggesting mischievous children

indicators.note: twister signals that the letters of treat are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: Mischievous children demonstrating how to make a tornado-shaped sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twister' rearranges TREAT as TRATE after DEMONS.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain by practical example is to illustrate a method.
